title: Personal Credit Cards: Applications, Underwriting and Tier Changes
content:
This page governs how an application for Personal Credit Cards is taken and decided, what an approval sets, how a Secured Visa graduates, and when a cardholder may move between tiers.

## Applications

An application names the tier requested and is recorded with status applied. The applicant's age is measured in whole years completed on the application date, using the date of birth held on the customer profile; it must reach the tier's youngest accepted age and, for a tier that has an upper age, must not pass it. The age requirement is judged against the tier's limits on the application date and from the bank's profile record, not from what the applicant states.

- Visa Infinite Private Client may be opened only by an applicant who holds a Private Client Checking account in active status, as shown in the bank's checking records.
- Secured Visa needs a security deposit no smaller than the tier's smallest accepted deposit, and the credit limit of a Secured Visa is always the amount of deposit held.

## Underwriting decisions

Approval and decline are made by the credit system's underwriting; the agent never makes either decision. An approval activates the account and sets:

- a credit limit between the tier's lowest and highest limits;
- a purchase APR within the tier's range, and the tier's own cash advance APR;
- on tiers that offer an introductory balance transfer rate, an end date for that rate equal to the statement closing date of the cycle whose position after opening matches the tier's number of introductory cycles.

A declined or withdrawn application closes without becoming an account in use.

## Secured Visa graduation

A Secured Visa is reviewed when it reaches the tier's graduation review point in months after opening. It graduates into the tier's target tier when each of its last six statements was paid on time, meaning that for each of those statements the payments and credits posted between its closing date and its due date reached its minimum payment, counted as an unbroken run from the most recent due date backward. On graduation the credit limit is kept and the security deposit is returned, paid out to one of the customer's PCB accounts or sent as an official check.

## Other tier changes

A cardholder may ask to move to another tier only where both tiers share the same rewards currency. No change is made into or out of Secured Visa. A tier change keeps the account's limit, APR and balance.

> Hypothetical illustration: a cardholder of College Rewards Visa, a cash back tier, may ask to move to Cash Rewards Visa, another cash back tier, and keeps the same limit, APR and balance; a move from College Rewards Visa to Travel Rewards Visa Signature, a points tier, is not available.
